title: Dynamic batch governor with predictive GPU headroom and KV-tier safeguards
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a dynamic micro-batching governor that combines a short-term QPS predictor, GPU slab headroom telemetry, and multi-tier KV cache safeguards to reduce 95th percentile latency spikes and avoid OOM/eviction storms under sudden high-QPS bursts.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile request latency across representative workloads reduced by >= 15% during 2x sustained QPS spikes compared to baseline
KV cache hotset eviction churn reduced by >= 25% under the same spike scenarios
No GPU OOMs in canary across 72h with synthetic spike tests (2x baseline QPS bursts every 15 minutes)
Per-route headroom gauge and admission signal visible in Console with 1s resolution
Graceful degradation path exercised: when admission fails, lower-cost quantized variant used with documented quality delta
design_notes: Use an autoregressive short-window QPS predictor (EWMA + short AR(3)) to anticipate 1-6s ahead arrival rate changes rather than only instantaneous queue length
Leverage GPU slab allocator metrics (free slab bytes, active slab count, allocation rate) to compute a smoothed headroom score; map to discrete ticket sizes for admission decisions

Introduce KV-tiering: hot (in-GPU KV), warm (pinned in CPU DRAM with fast memcpy), cold (SSD-backed async spill). Admission respects hotset preservation by probabilistically denying low-priority requests when hot hit-rate risk exceeds threshold

Admission controller produces a 3-bit decision: admit-full, admit-reduced (truncate/max-tokens clamp + quantized model), queue, reject-backpressure. Decisions flow through existing grpc backpressure header semantics
Primary control loop runs at 100ms cadence; slower learner updates (10s) adjust thresholds using simulated replay traces for stability
implementation_notes: Add predictor module to request router; maintain per-route short-history (20 samples) with bounded memory
Expose new GPU headroom Prometheus metrics: gpu_headroom_score, gpu_slab_free_bytes, gpu_alloc_rate; tag by node and model-variant
Admission controller extends existing microbatch admission codepath with a fast-path that checks precomputed ticket map to select microbatch size and token cap
KV-tier manager implemented as a policy layer that annotates requests with desired kv_tier and prefetch hints; eviction scheduler will respect kv_tier priorities
Fallback quantized variants should be loaded in warm pools to avoid cold load latencies; use async preload based on predictor signals
Simulator harness: integrate with existing burst-sim tool but add KV-tier model and GPU slab allocator behavior calibrated from perf lab traces
rollout_plan: Feature gating behind runtime flag (dynamic_batch_governor) and per-customer opt-in
Stage 1 (canary): enable on 5 low-traffic nodes with synthetic spike script for 48h
Stage 2 (beta): enable for 10% of internal hosted traffic and monitor headroom gauge, KV hit-rate, 95p latency for 7 days
Stage 3 (gradual): expand to customers with autoscaling disabled (Dedicated private beta) and run A/B against baseline for cost and latency comparisons
Emergency kill-switch: revert admission to baseline microbatching and trigger immediate model fallback to last-stable variant
testing_plan: Unit tests for predictor (edge cases: cold start, bursty warmup, clock skew)
Integration tests in sim harness verifying admission decisions under synthetic patterns (ramp, sawtooth, Poisson bursts)
Chaos test: simulate KV-tier SSD latency spikes and validate no OOM and acceptable latency degradation
Load test: 10k req/s mixed prompt lengths with 2x burst every 15 minutes across 48h in staging
Regression: ensure token-cost delta < 5% for admitted-reduced path compared to full path on representative prompts
